handBrain.title: What is Hand+Brain?
handBrain.intro: Hand+Brain is a collaborative chess variant where a human and engine work together as a team. One partner is the "Brain" (chooses WHICH piece type to move) and the other is the "Hand" (chooses WHERE to move it).
handBrain.normalBrain: The engine suggests a piece type (e.g., "Knight").
handBrain.normalHand: You choose any legal move using that piece type.
handBrain.normalNote: Great for learning strategy from the engine's piece selection.
handBrain.reverseBrain: You lift and replace a piece to select its type.
handBrain.reverseHand: The engine finds the best move with that piece, shown via LEDs.
handBrain.reverseNote: Great for practicing piece coordination while engine handles tactics.

debug.title: Debug
debug.intro: Serial debug logging records the raw communication between the Raspberry Pi and the board controller during startup. Enable it, reboot the board to capture the startup handshake, then download the log and send it to support. This helps diagnose boards that never finish starting up — for example, a v1 board whose LED circles keep spinning. Leaving it on makes the log grow quickly.

displayTuning.descriptionUc8151d: If a replacement panel ghosts, smears, or looks faint on partial updates (e.g. the clock), try a different waveform profile. Full refresh always uses the panel's built-in waveform; only the partial-refresh waveform changes. Each selection applies immediately with a full refresh -- no reboot.
displayTuning.descriptionSsd16xx: If the panel is blank, faint, or ghosted, try a different waveform profile. Each selection is applied immediately with a full refresh -- no reboot -- so you can compare them and keep the one that produces a clean image.
displayTuning.waveformHelp: The recipe used to drive the panel. Built-In uses the panel's own factory waveform; the others load a known manufacturer table.
displayTuning.batchHelp: Coalesce a rapid burst of screen updates into a single refresh of the final frame. When updates arrive faster than the e-paper can redraw, this skips the intermediate frames so the display shows the latest state instead of lagging behind. Turn off to draw every intermediate frame (slower when updates come quickly, but shows each step). Recommended on.
displayTuning.highContrastHelp: Drive the VCOM/source voltages harder than the profile's defaults to darken a faint image. Try this if the image draws but only faintly. Not a datasheet-backed setting; leave off if the display already looks good.
displayTuning.threeColorHelp: For red/white/black panels only. Highlights checks, threatened queens, the game result, and losing evaluation bars in red. Red ink can only change with a full refresh, so those red updates take ~12-15 seconds; ordinary moves stay fast.
displayTuning.savedOffline: Saved. It will apply when the board is running.
displayTuning.threeColorOn: Three-color mode on. Red highlights refresh in ~12-15s; normal moves stay fast.
displayTuning.applied: Applied. The panel refreshed with the new setting.

licenses.title: Open Source Licenses
licenses.intro: Universal Chess is open source software built on the shoulders of giants. Below are the licenses for this project and its dependencies.

items.universalChess: The main project. Universal Chess provides a modern web interface and enhanced software for DGT smart chess boards, enabling play against engines, online opponents, and game analysis.
items.dgtcentaurMods: The original open source project that Universal Chess is built upon. DGTCentaur Mods pioneered custom software for the DGT Centaur chess board.
items.reactChessboard: Renders the interactive chess board in the web interface. Provides drag-and-drop piece movement, board orientation, custom arrows, and smooth animations.
items.chessPiecesOnebit: One-bit 16x16 pixel-art chess piece sprites used by the "onebit" e-paper board sprite style. Released into the public domain (CC0); attribution provided as a courtesy.
items.cburnett: The classic Cburnett/Wikimedia vector chess set, rasterised to a 16x16 sprite sheet. It is the default e-paper board sprite style (shown as "Default"); the previous DGTCentaur Mods set is still available as "Original Mods". Multi-licensed by the author under GPLv2+, GFDL and a BSD-style license; used here under the BSD option.
items.stockfish: The default chess engine for play and analysis. Stockfish is the strongest open source chess engine, providing move evaluation, best move suggestions, and opponent play.
items.stockfishJs: Stockfish 16 compiled to WebAssembly, used only by the optional Deep Analysis setting. Nothing is distributed with this project: when you enable the setting, your browser downloads the engine, its WebAssembly and its neural network (about 39 MB in total) directly from the jsDelivr CDN at the pinned version stockfish@16.0.0, and each file is checked against a recorded SHA-256 before it runs. Licensed under the GPL-3.0; the corresponding source is at the linked repository.
items.reckless: An optionally installable chess engine written in Rust with an embedded NNUE evaluation, consistently among the strongest engines in CCC and TCEC. Installed binaries are built from an unmodified upstream release; the corresponding source is available at the linked repository under the AGPL-3.0.
items.react: The UI framework powering the web interface. React enables the component-based architecture, reactive state management, and efficient DOM updates.
items.vite: The build tool and development server. Vite provides fast hot module replacement during development and optimized production builds.
items.chartjs: Renders the evaluation graph showing position advantage over time. Displays engine evaluation history as an interactive chart during game review.
items.zustand: Manages global application state. Zustand handles game state synchronization, connection status, and settings across all components.
items.waveshareEpaper: Source of the SSD1680 (GDEM029T94) waveform tables and init for the V1-panel driver and the "Waveshare 2.9″ V2" profile, and of the UC8151D partial LUTs/analog bytes (epd2in9d.py) used by the default "Waveshare 2.9″ V2 — UC8151D" profile.
items.gxepd2: Arduino e-paper library by Jean-Marc Zingg. Verbatim source of the IL3820/GDEH029A1 LUTs (class GxEPD2_290), the DEPG0290BS register partial LUT (GxEPD2_290_BS), and the UC8151D variant partial LUTs/analog bytes — GDEW029I6FD (GxEPD2_290_I6FD), T5D (GxEPD2_290_T5D) and the experimental GDEW029M06 (GxEPD2_290_M06) — used by the tuning profiles; also corroborates the GDEM029T94 table and the panel-OTP approach.
items.goodDisplay: Original vendor demo code (relayed verbatim via GxEPD2) behind the IL3820/GDEH029A1, DEPG0290BS, GDEW029I6FD, GDEW029M06 and T5D tuning profiles.
